summary: Snapshot s04 is an older AF_XDP tree (pre-6.8): no xsk_tx_metadata struct, no XDP_TXMD_FLAGS, no tx_metadata_len anywhere in the tree; the seed path does not exist here. Core TX descriptor fetch uses single struct assignment into kernel memory followed by validation on the same copy (xskq_cons_read_desc line 199-200; batch variant line 224-225) and validated copies are what drivers consume (desc.addr/desc.len from stack/pool->tx_descs). Checked all 8 AF_XDP-capable driver TX paths (ixgbe, i40e, ice, igc, mlx5, nfp, dpaa2, stmmac) plus net/xdp generic xmit; all consume the locally snapshotted desc. Residual risk is compiler-mediated tearing of the 16-byte struct copy from shared memory (no READ_ONCE), a hardening gap but not the seed's double-fetch pattern. FQ fill-ring addr path uses *addr = ring->desc[idx] unchecked by design (addr re-validated later at xp_assign_dev / xp_raw_get_data). No reportable validate-then-reread on UMEM-resident fields found.

FQ addr read unchecked by design; address only becomes a kernel pointer later via xp_assign_dev/xp_raw_get_data after chunk-index validation, and RX side re-checks len against frame size.
